findings.problem: The previous workbench helper treated budget zero as complete, omitted service area and counted granted consultation consent as sufficient for appointment.
findings.trigger: Create a lead with all identity/building/intent/stage fields, budgetCents=0, no serviceArea and consultation-only granted consent.
findings.impact: A card could understate missing information while the native handoff operation still required the missing fields and appointment purpose.
findings.currentBehavior: leadMissing uses native completeness; the compatibility fallback implements the same positive-budget, service-area and two-purpose checks.

findings.problem: Schema id fields originally rendered employee and skill IDs as plain text inputs, despite the catalogue containing Chinese role names and skill titles.
findings.trigger: Launch sales-coach employee-work from the team page, then select appointment-coordinator.
findings.impact: A user needed internal IDs and could keep a skill belonging to a previous role.
findings.currentBehavior: field builds catalogue-backed Chinese role/skill selects and syncSkillOptions clears incompatible values and filters the selected role skills.

findings.problem: The old PostgreSQL seeder regression expected 20 roles/35 skills after the industry bundle added seven roles and fourteen skills.
findings.trigger: Run the required PostgreSQL seeder suite with the current sealed bundle.
findings.impact: The native database gate would fail on an intentional workforce expansion; counts alone would also miss wrong installed bodies.
findings.currentBehavior: The seeder test requires 27 roles/49 skills, SQL-checks every new role and its two skills and compares all fourteen installed SOP bodies byte-for-byte with their declared source.

source.test: first seed, repeat and concurrent repeat have exact assets and no business events

findings.problem: The manifest default UI declared only nineteen objects and four workflows while the native runtime/schema already contained twenty-seven objects and five workflows.
findings.trigger: Load the default smart-home bundle through loadBundleUiProjection.
findings.impact: The base client projection would omit the eight new dossier/engineering/contract/business object labels and the employee-work workflow label.
findings.currentBehavior: The industry manifest now has all schema labels and the employee task workflow; the actual base projection returns the exact 27/5 labels.

verification.actual: 27 exact object labels / 5 exact workflow labels

conclusions.statement: The ordinary CLI scenario importer uses an operator in cli with humanConfirmed=false; init --demo uses seedSyntheticScenario. It does not create owner terminal approval.
The stdio MCP server calls the runtime as an agent. scenario.import is not exposed to that role; catalogue-derived read methods remain separate from human-call methods.

The PostgreSQL seeder reads declared sealed industry context and creates only its explicit sandbox identity/assets. It rejects production, provenance collisions, altered assets and conflicting installation data in a transaction.
conclusions.boundaries: The selected bundle-loading call chain was read; unrelated shared gateways/model routes were not audited.

conclusions.statement: The capability generator gives README the default smart-home product group, keeps broader inherited engineering capabilities in their labelled guide and links current-task screenshots/evidence. capabilityStatus does not turn discovery metadata into verified runtime availability.
The workbench shows model proposals separately from applied customer facts, draws point plans from persisted millimetre geometry, and retains terminal-established human sessions for human operations.

Current metadata validates all 122 declared sealed assets; native registries equal the runtime 51 operations/5 workflows, and the executed base projection equals the current 27 object labels/5 workflow labels.
